title: Will Bayley loses his world title to Yan Shuo as Aaron McKibbin beats illness to guarantee a medal in Pattaya
seo_title: World Para Championships: Bayley loses title to Yan Shuo
description: Will Bayley's class 7 world title defence ended against Yan Shuo in Pattaya, while Aaron McKibbin came back from illness to reach the class 8 semi-finals.
standfirst: A flu-hit Bayley lost a quarter-final worthy of a final to his Chinese rival, while McKibbin, who had not trained since Thursday, saved his best for a deciding game against Maksym Nikolenko.
body: Will Bayley's reign as men's class 7 world champion is over. The world No 1, who had been fighting flu for two days, lost 3-1 to China's Yan Shuo in the quarter-finals of the World Para Championships in Pattaya on Monday.
On the same day Aaron McKibbin, who had pulled out of the doubles through illness, won two singles matches to reach the men's class 8 semi-finals and guarantee himself a medal.
## A final played in the quarter-finals

Yan beat Bayley in the last two Paralympic finals, but Bayley had won both their meetings this year. The Chinese two-time Paralympic champion's ranking meant he needed a wild card to enter the championships and was unseeded, so the two met in Bayley's first match.

Yan won the first four points. Bayley, 37, recovered to take the opening game 11-7 and fought back from 10-8 down in the second to 10-10, but after he called a timeout Yan took the game 12-10. Yan won the third 11-7, and although Bayley led 4-2 in the fourth and saved a match point at 10-8 with a serve, Yan closed it out 11-9 on the next.

"If you don't take your chances at this level you do get punished and I don't think I took my chances when I really had to," Bayley said. "It would have been a great final and it is just disappointing to play Yan in a quarterfinal when we've played two Paralympic finals."

Bayley had already won mixed doubles bronze with Bly Twomey earlier in the championships, as Eleven [reported on Saturday](/news/world-para-championships-2026-doubles-bronze-bayley-twomey-ryan-matthews.html).
## McKibbin wins on his second match point

McKibbin, 34, had not trained since the previous Thursday. He beat Israel's Yehonatan Levi, the 17-year-old world No 15, 11-8, 6-11, 11-7, 11-6 in the last 16, and returned a few hours later to face Ukraine's Maksym Nikolenko, the world No 7 and a bronze medallist at Tokyo and Paris.

Nikolenko led 2-1 after taking the second and third games 11-5. McKibbin levelled with an 11-8 fourth game, and the decider swung both ways: Nikolenko led 3-1, McKibbin led 7-4, and it was 9-9 before McKibbin missed a first match point at 10-9. A net cord gave him a second at 11-10, and Nikolenko put a backhand long.
"I've been in bed for 48 hours and I've eaten five pieces of bread in the last two days, but it got to the point where I just wanted to try and play in the singles," McKibbin said.

He plays Italy's Ludovico Bini, who beat him 3-0 in Slovenia, in the semi-finals on Wednesday, and took Tuesday off to rest. "I feel like I'm about 50% today so if I have another full day to recover and I can arrive at the semi at 70 or 80% I'll be over the moon," he said.
## Ryan and Morizono into the quarter-finals

Chris Ryan came from a game down to beat Egypt's Ahmed Elmahsy, the world No 8, 3-1 in the men's class 2 last 16. Ryan was 5-2 down in the second game when he lost a point for a foul serve, and from 6-2 down he won the next five points on his way to taking it 11-8. He won the third 11-5 and the fourth 11-7, after Elmahsy had saved four match points from 10-3.

"I had next to no feeling in the first set. A lot of my game is based on touch, and it wasn't there at the start," Ryan said. His quarter-final, on Tuesday, was against Slovakia's Peter Lovas, a former world No 1 who had knocked out the current No 1, Park Jin Cheol.

Joshua Morizono beat the American Tahl Leibovitz, a former Paralympic champion, 12-10, 11-7, 10-12, 10-12, 11-9 in the men's class 9 last 16, having led 9-5 in the decider and seen it cut to 9-8. "The result is the main thing especially at a major," he said. He meets Ukraine's Lev Kats in the quarter-finals on Wednesday.
## Perry and Shilton go out

Martin Perry led 10-5 in the first game against the 17-year-old American Samuel Altshuler, the world No 6, but lost six points in a row and went down 12-10, 11-4, 10-12, 11-3 in the men's class 6 last 16. "The first set was massive," Perry said.

Billy Shilton lost 11-7, 11-7, 11-9 to Poland's Piotr Grudzien, the world No 4, in the men's class 8 last 16, having led in all three games. All the events in Pattaya are straight knockouts, so both are out of the singles.
McKibbin's semi-final against Bini and Morizono's quarter-final against Kats are both on Wednesday.
